title: Sulfurihydrogenibium proteomics
projectDescription: To understand the ecophysiology of Sulfurihydrogenibium spp. in situ, integrated metagenomic, metatranscriptomic and metaproteomic analyses were conducted on a microbial community from Narrow Gauge at Mammoth Hot Springs, Yellowstone National Park.
sampleProcessingProtocol: Total bacterial proteins were separated by SDS-PAGE, folowed by in-gel trypsination. The extracted peptides  were analyzed by mass spectrometry.
dataProcessingProtocol: The mass spectrometry data was analyzed by an automated proteomics pipeline (APP, (Malm et al, 2014), which first utilizes several open source search engines (e.g. X!tandem, MyriMatch, MSGFplus and Comet), followed by validation and compilation of peptides/proteins using PeptideProphet, iProphet and ProteinProphet.
